source.text: Παῦλος καὶ Σιλουανὸς καὶ Τιμόθεος τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ Θεσσαλονικέων ἐν θεῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ·

records.literal_gloss: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of [the] Thessalonians in God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ;

en.L: Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: From Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians, which belongs to God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: This letter is from Paul, Silvanus and Timothy. We are writing to the church in the city of Thessalonica. You belong to God our Father and to the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Paul et Silvain et Timothée, à l’église des Thessaloniciens en Dieu notre Père et le Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: De la part de Paul, Silvain et Timothée, à l’église des Thessaloniciens, qui appartient à Dieu notre Père et au Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de Paul, de Silvain et de Timothée. Nous écrivons à l’église de la ville de Thessalonique. Vous appartenez à Dieu notre Père et au Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

decisions.choice: the same senders and church as 1 Thessalonians
decisions.reason: The opening repeats 1 Thessalonians 1:1 almost word for word. This letter follows up the first: the church is still under pressure (1:4), and some are now troubled by a claim that the day of the Lord has already come (2:1-2).

decisions.choice: in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: the church lives in union with them
decisions.reason: As in 1 Thessalonians 1:1, one preposition covers God and Jesus together; here Paul adds "our" Father.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: which belongs to
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "in God" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: "Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" (L), "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" (B, R); "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" with the article outside the span; "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}" for "in Christ" (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Thessalonians and Colossians: French cannot say "en Messie", so the span for "in Christ" covers the preposition; elsewhere the article stays outside the span. "Jésus Christ" is written without the usual hyphen so that both options read naturally.

decisions.choice: l’église des Thessaloniciens, lowercase (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: One congregation, the believers in Thessalonica, so "église" without the capital French keeps for the whole body of believers; the same for "les églises de Dieu" in 1:4.

source.text: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Grace to you and peace from God Father and Lord Jesus Christ.

en.L: Grace to you and peace from God [the] Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Grace and peace to you from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: We pray that God the Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will show you grace and give you peace.

fr.L: Grâce à vous et paix de la part de Dieu le Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Grâce et paix à vous de la part de Dieu le Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Nous prions pour que Dieu le Père et le Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} vous accordent la grâce et la paix.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "God the Father"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "God our Father", as in verse 1 and Paul's other greetings. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: We pray that God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ will show you grace and give you peace
alternatives: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable makes the greeting a prayer, as in 1 Thessalonians 1:1.

source.text: Εὐχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν τῷ θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί, καθὼς ἄξιόν ἐστιν, ὅτι ὑπεραυξάνει ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καὶ πλεονάζει ἡ ἀγάπη ἑνὸς ἑκάστου πάντων ὑμῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους, ὥστε αὐτοὺς ἡμᾶς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐγκαυχᾶσθαι ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τοῦ θεοῦ ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ὑμῶν καὶ πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς διωγμοῖς ὑμῶν καὶ ταῖς θλίψεσιν αἷς ἀνέχεσθε, ἔνδειγμα τῆς δικαίας κρίσεως τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ καταξιωθῆναι ὑμᾶς τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑπὲρ ἧς καὶ πάσχετε, εἴπερ δίκαιον παρὰ θεῷ ἀνταποδοῦναι τοῖς θλίβουσιν ὑμᾶς θλῖψιν καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς θλιβομένοις ἄνεσιν μεθ’ ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ μετ’ ἀγγέλων δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ ἐν φλογὶ πυρός, διδόντος ἐκδίκησιν τοῖς μὴ εἰδόσι θεὸν καὶ τοῖς μὴ ὑπακούουσιν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ, οἵτινες δίκην τίσουσιν ὄλεθρον αἰώνιον ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ, ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐνδοξασθῆναι ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ καὶ θαυμασθῆναι ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς πιστεύσασιν, ὅτι ἐπιστεύθη τὸ μαρτύριον ἡμῶν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: To give thanks we ought to the God always concerning you, brothers, just as fitting it is, because grows exceedingly the faith of you and increases the love of one each of all of you toward one another, \v 4 so that ourselves us in you to boast in the churches of the God for the endurance of you and faith in all the persecutions of you and the afflictions which you are bearing, \v 5 evidence of the just judgment of the God, so that to be counted worthy you of the kingdom of the God, for which also you suffer, \v 6 since [it is] just with God to repay to those afflicting you affliction \v 7 and to you, the [ones] being afflicted, relief with us at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with angels of power of him \v 8 in flame of fire, giving vengeance to those not knowing God and to those not obeying the gospel of the Lord of us Jesus, \v 9 who [the] penalty will pay, destruction eternal, away from [the] face of the Lord and from the glory of the strength of him, \v 10 when he comes to be glorified in the holy [ones] of him and to be marveled at in all those having believed, because was believed the testimony of us to you, in the day that.

en.L: We ought always to give thanks to God for you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, as is fitting, because your faith is growing greatly and the love of each one of you all for one another is increasing, \v 4 so that we ourselves boast about you in the churches of God for your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and the afflictions that you are bearing. \v 5 [This is] evidence of the just judgment of God, so that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are also suffering, \v 6 since [it is] just in God's sight to repay with affliction those who afflict you, \v 7 and [to give] relief to you who are afflicted, along with us, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power \v 8 in flaming fire, inflicting vengeance on those who do not know God and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus. \v 9 They will pay the penalty, eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} might, \v 10 when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to be glorified in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy ones and to be marveled at among all who have believed (because our testimony to you was believed) on that day.
en.B: We are bound to thank God for you at all times, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, and rightly so, because your faith is growing beyond measure and the love every one of you has for the others keeps increasing. \v 4 So we ourselves speak proudly of you among the churches of God, because of your endurance and faith in all the persecutions and troubles you are bearing. \v 5 All this is evidence that God judges rightly, and the result will be that you are counted worthy of God's kingdom, for which you are suffering. \v 6 For it is right for God to repay with suffering those who make you suffer, \v 7 and to give rest to you who suffer, as to us also, when the Lord Jesus appears from heaven with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty angels \v 8 in a blaze of fire, bringing punishment on those who do not know God and on those who refuse to obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus. \v 9 They will pay the penalty of eternal destruction, cut off from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power, \v 10 on that day when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to be glorified among {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people and marveled at by all who believed. And you are among those believers, for when we bore witness to you, you believed it.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we should always thank God for you. It is right for us to do this, because your faith is growing more and more, and every one of you loves the others more and more. \v 4 So we tell all of God's churches how proud we are of you. We tell them how you keep going and keep your faith, even though people are hurting you and you are going through hard times. \v 5 This shows that God judges fairly. God will count you worthy to be part of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom, the kingdom you are suffering for. \v 6 God is fair. He will pay back with trouble the people who are troubling you. \v 7 And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give rest to you who are suffering, and to us too. This will happen when the Lord Jesus comes from heaven with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} powerful angels \v 8 in flames of fire. He will punish those who do not know God and those who do not obey the good news about our Lord Jesus. \v 9 Their punishment will be eternal destruction. They will be shut out from the Lord's presence and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious power \v 10 on the day when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes. On that day all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people will give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory, and all who have believed will be amazed at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And you will be among them, because you believed what we told you.

fr.L: Nous devons toujours rendre grâce à Dieu pour vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, comme il convient, parce que votre foi grandit beaucoup et que l’amour de chacun de vous tous les uns pour les autres augmente, \v 4 de sorte que nous-mêmes, nous nous glorifions de vous dans les églises de Dieu, pour votre persévérance et votre foi dans toutes vos persécutions et les afflictions que vous supportez. \v 5 [C’est] une preuve du juste jugement de Dieu, pour que vous soyez jugés dignes du royaume de Dieu, pour lequel aussi vous souffrez, \v 6 puisqu’il est juste aux yeux de Dieu de rendre l’affliction à ceux qui vous affligent, \v 7 et [de donner] à vous qui êtes affligés le repos avec nous, lors de la révélation du Seigneur Jésus depuis le ciel avec les anges de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance, \v 8 dans une flamme de feu, infligeant la vengeance à ceux qui ne connaissent pas Dieu et à ceux qui n’obéissent pas à l’Évangile de notre Seigneur Jésus. \v 9 Ils subiront [comme] peine une destruction éternelle, loin de la face du Seigneur et de la gloire de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} force, \v 10 quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra pour être glorifié dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} saints et admiré parmi tous ceux qui ont cru (parce que notre témoignage auprès de vous a été cru), en ce jour-là.
fr.B: Nous devons rendre grâce à Dieu pour vous en tout temps, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, comme il est juste, car votre foi grandit au-delà de toute mesure, et l’amour que chacun de vous a pour les autres ne cesse d’augmenter. \v 4 Aussi, nous-mêmes, nous parlons de vous avec fierté dans les églises de Dieu, à cause de votre persévérance et de votre foi au milieu de toutes les persécutions et de toutes les épreuves que vous supportez. \v 5 Tout cela prouve que Dieu juge avec justice, et il en résultera que vous serez jugés dignes du royaume de Dieu, pour lequel vous souffrez. \v 6 Car il est juste pour Dieu de rendre la souffrance à ceux qui vous font souffrir, \v 7 et de vous donner le repos, à vous qui souffrez, comme à nous aussi, quand le Seigneur Jésus apparaîtra du ciel avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges puissants, \v 8 dans un feu flamboyant, pour punir ceux qui ne connaissent pas Dieu et ceux qui refusent d’obéir à l’Évangile de notre Seigneur Jésus. \v 9 Ils subiront la peine d’une destruction éternelle, coupés de la présence du Seigneur et de la gloire de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance, \v 10 le jour où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra pour être glorifié au milieu de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple saint et admiré par tous ceux qui ont cru. Et vous êtes de ces croyants, car lorsque nous vous avons rendu témoignage, vous l’avez cru.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, nous devons toujours remercier Dieu pour vous. Il est juste que nous le fassions, parce que votre foi grandit de plus en plus, et que chacun de vous aime les autres de plus en plus. \v 4 Alors nous disons à toutes les églises de Dieu combien nous sommes fiers de vous. Nous leur racontons comment vous tenez bon et gardez votre foi, même quand des gens vous font du mal et que vous passez par des moments difficiles. \v 5 Cela montre que Dieu juge avec justice. Dieu vous jugera dignes de faire partie de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume, ce royaume pour lequel vous souffrez. \v 6 Dieu est juste. Il rendra le mal à ceux qui vous font du mal. \v 7 Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous donnera le repos, à vous qui souffrez, et à nous aussi. Cela arrivera quand le Seigneur Jésus viendra du ciel avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges puissants, \v 8 au milieu des flammes. Il punira ceux qui ne connaissent pas Dieu et ceux qui n’obéissent pas à la bonne nouvelle de notre Seigneur Jésus. \v 9 Leur punition sera une destruction éternelle. Ils seront mis à l’écart de la présence du Seigneur et de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance glorieuse, \v 10 le jour où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra. Ce jour-là, tout {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple saint {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendra gloire, et tous ceux qui ont cru seront émerveillés devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Et vous serez parmi eux, parce que vous avez cru ce que nous vous avons dit.

decisions.choice: we ought to give thanks: a duty, gladly owned
decisions.reason: ὀφείλομεν ("we ought") speaks of an obligation: their growth makes thanks the only fitting response, ἄξιόν ἐστιν ("as is fitting").

decisions.choice: faith growing, love increasing: Paul's earlier prayer answered
decisions.reason: In 1 Thessalonians 3:10-12 Paul prayed that their faith would be supplied and their love increase. ὑπεραυξάνω is a strong word: growing beyond measure.

decisions.choice: evidence of God's just judgment: their faithful endurance under suffering shows that God's coming judgment will be just
alternatives: the persecution itself is a sign that judgment is coming on the persecutors
decisions.reason: ἔνδειγμα stands loosely after verse 4 and most naturally refers to the whole situation: their faith holding firm in suffering is a sign that God is at work and will judge rightly, vindicating them and repaying their persecutors (verses 6-7; Philippians 1:28).

decisions.choice: counted worthy of the kingdom: declared fit by God, not earning it
decisions.reason: καταξιόω means to count or declare worthy. Their suffering for the kingdom marks them as belonging to it (compare verse 11).

decisions.choice: God's justice repays: affliction to those who afflict, relief to the afflicted
decisions.reason: Paul leaves repayment to God, who alone judges rightly (Romans 12:19). The relief (ἄνεσιν, rest) is for Paul and his companions too.

decisions.choice: the revelation of the Lord Jesus: his unveiling, when he comes
decisions.reason: ἀποκαλύψει is an unveiling: Jesus, now hidden from sight, will be seen (1 Corinthians 1:7).

decisions.choice: in flaming fire: the fire of God's appearing
decisions.reason: God appeared in a flame of fire at the bush (Exodus 3:2) and "will come in fire" to judge (Isaiah 66:15). Some manuscripts reverse the two nouns ("in fire of flame"); the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: vengeance: punishment that puts wrong right
decisions.reason: ἐκδίκησιν is justice carried out on wrongdoers, which belongs to God (Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19). Here Jesus carries it out.

decisions.choice: those who do not know God and those who do not obey the gospel
decisions.reason: The repeated article could mark two groups (Gentiles who do not know God, Jeremiah 10:25, and those who reject the gospel) or describe one group in two ways. Either way, the punishment is for refusing God.

decisions.choice: away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his might: Isaiah 2:10, 2:19, 2:21
alternatives: destruction coming from the Lord's presence
decisions.reason: The words echo Isaiah 2, where people hide "from the presence of the LORD and from the glory of his majesty". ἀπὸ can mean separation ("away from") or source ("coming from"). The echo of Isaiah suggests being banished from the Lord's presence, the opposite of being "with the Lord" for ever (1 Thessalonians 4:17).

decisions.choice: eternal destruction: ruin that belongs to the age to come and has no end
decisions.reason: ὄλεθρον is ruin, as in 1 Thessalonians 5:3; αἰώνιον ties it to the age to come, as "eternal life" is.

decisions.choice: because our testimony was believed: the Thessalonians are among those believers
decisions.reason: The clause breaks into the sentence to include the readers: the "all who have believed" of that day will include them, because they believed what Paul told them.

decisions.choice: to be glorified in his holy ones: his glory seen in his people
alternatives: to be glorified by his holy ones
decisions.reason: ἐν ("in") most naturally means his glory will shine in and through his people, as in verse 12; it may also mean "among them".

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: cut off from (B); shut out from (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m10, which is uncertain; Literal keeps "away from".

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable divide the sentence and put the clause about the Thessalonians at the end
alternatives: one sentence from verse 3 to verse 10
decisions.reason: The Greek runs from verse 3 to verse 10 as one sentence. Balanced and Readable divide it into shorter sentences and move the clause about the readers (m12) to the end, where it reads naturally.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: 2 Thessalonians is a letter: Paul speaks to the readers about what they believed and were taught ("vous avez cru", "nous vous avons dit"), and French uses the passé composé for that, as in 1 Thessalonians.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in English, the church is addressed as women and men together; "frères" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Thessalonians: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for God or Christ carries the span wherever the English "he" does; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital ("Il punira").

decisions.choice: l’Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Thessalonians and the English: Readable says "good news", since "Évangile" is church language.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} saints (L); {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple saint (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms: here the holy ones are his people, in whom his glory is seen (m13), so Balanced and Readable say so, as the English "holy people" does.

source.text: εἰς ὃ καὶ προσευχόμεθα πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν, ἵνα ὑμᾶς ἀξιώσῃ τῆς κλήσεως ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν καὶ πληρώσῃ πᾶσαν εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης καὶ ἔργον πίστεως ἐν δυνάμει, ὅπως ἐνδοξασθῇ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν αὐτῷ, κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: for which also we pray always for you, that you may count worthy of the calling the God of us and may fulfill every desire of goodness and work of faith with power, \v 12 so that may be glorified the name of the Lord of us Jesus in you, and you in him, according to the grace of the God of us and Lord Jesus Christ.

en.L: To this end we also pray always for you, that our God may count you worthy of the calling and fulfill every desire for goodness and work of faith with power, \v 12 so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, according to the grace of our God and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: With this in view we pray for you constantly. We ask our God to count you worthy of the life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called you to, and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power to fulfill every good desire you have and every work your faith takes on. \v 12 Then the name of our Lord Jesus will be honored in you, and you will be honored in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, by the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: So we always pray for you. We ask our God to make you worthy of the life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has called you to live. We ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to use {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power to help you do all the good things you want to do, and all the things your faith leads you to do. \v 12 Then people will honor the name of our Lord Jesus because of you, and you will be honored because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. All this comes from the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: À cette fin aussi, nous prions toujours pour vous, afin que notre Dieu vous juge dignes de l’appel et accomplisse avec puissance tout désir de bonté et toute œuvre de foi, \v 12 afin que le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus soit glorifié en vous, et vous en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, selon la grâce de notre Dieu et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Dans cette perspective, nous prions sans cesse pour vous. Nous demandons à notre Dieu de vous juger dignes de la vie à laquelle {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a appelés, et d’accomplir par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance tout bon désir que vous avez et toute œuvre qu’entreprend votre foi. \v 12 Ainsi le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus sera honoré en vous, et vous serez honorés en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, par la grâce de notre Dieu et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que nous prions toujours pour vous. Nous demandons à notre Dieu de vous rendre dignes de la vie qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a appelés à vivre. Nous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandons d’utiliser {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance pour vous aider à faire tout le bien que vous voulez faire, et tout ce que votre foi vous pousse à faire. \v 12 Alors les gens honoreront le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus à cause de vous, et vous serez honorés parce que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenez. Tout cela vient de la grâce de notre Dieu et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

decisions.choice: to this end: with that day in view
decisions.reason: εἰς ὃ looks back to verse 10: Paul prays that they will be ready to share in Christ's glory.

decisions.choice: count worthy: consider and declare worthy
decisions.reason: ἀξιόω usually means to consider worthy. The prayer asks God to find them worthy of the calling he gave them (1 Thessalonians 2:12).

decisions.choice: every desire for goodness: their own desire to do good
decisions.reason: εὐδοκίαν can be God's good pleasure or a person's desire. Joined with "work of faith", it is most likely their desire to do good, which God brings to completion by his power.

decisions.choice: glorified in you, and you in him: each honored in the other
decisions.reason: Christ's name is honored through his people, and they share his honor (1:10).

decisions.choice: the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ: two persons, as in verse 2
alternatives: the grace of our God and Lord, Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: One article covers both nouns, which could mean that Jesus Christ is called "our God and Lord". But "Lord Jesus Christ" is used almost as a name, which often goes without the article, and verse 2 names God and the Lord Jesus Christ as two. Both readings are possible.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called you to (B); the life {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has called you to live (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the calling" is: the life God called them to.

decisions.choice: honored
decisions.reason: The verb here is not the key term for "glorify"; "honored" fits the mutual honor of m4.
